messages.author: d458018b8e47149d
messages.subject: importing .txt file into R
parts:
Hello,

I have tried to import a .txt file of model output data into Excel and R (using read.table) and convert using the delimiting tools but some of the column headers are 'stuck' together. For example: DA_STmmSURQ_GENmmSURQ_CNTmm is currently a header title that should be three different columns but the way Excel and R are reading it in, it keeps it and the data below it as one column. Any advice? I can go through manually and modify it but would obviously rather not do that and I can't really modify the way the output come out from the model. Thanks in advance.

I tried attaching the text file here but it wouldn't work, if you want, I can send it via email most likely.

messages.author: 80d591788d62f6ed
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: importing .txt file into R
parts:
You could try importing to R with no header and skipping the top row, something like: read.table("Your_file.txt", sep = "\t", header = FALSE, skip = 1)  
Then add your column names later with colnames(yourdata) <- c("Col1", "Col2", etc....)

Good luck, 
Eric

messages.author: 03c3aeeb0cc6692c
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: importing .txt file into R
parts: I agree with Eric that sounds like the best way if you don't want to manually edit it. But manually editing should be very easy, unless you have to do this for many many files. Just open your file up in Notepad++ and make sure all characters are visible. If it is tab delimited you can go to View/Show Symbol/Show white space and TAB, and then manually insert the tabs where they belong.

messages.subject: Re: importing .txt file into R
parts:
You want to use the read.fwf function (read fixed width format) - you have to give it a vector which each element is the width in # characters of each column. 

Matt
